prompt: Is import VAT always 12% for goods used to make export products?
answer:
### Short Answer
Import VAT on goods used to make export products is generally 12% as mandated by the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC).

### Controlling Authorities
The applicable provision is Section 107 of the NIRC, which states that there shall be levied, assessed, and collected a value-added tax equivalent to twelve percent (12%) on every importation of goods. This is further supported by Revenue Regulations No. 16-2005, which clarifies that any person importing goods is liable for the VAT imposed under Section 107.

### Interpretation
Section 107 of the NIRC explicitly establishes a 12% VAT on the importation of goods, which includes those intended for export production. Revenue Regulations No. 16-2005 reiterates this liability for VAT on imported goods, regardless of whether the goods are used in the course of trade or business. Therefore, the standard rate of 12% applies uniformly to all importations unless specific exemptions or zero-rating provisions apply.

### Practical Meaning
For businesses importing goods to manufacture export products, the 12% VAT will be applicable at the time of importation. However, if the exported products qualify for zero-rating under the provisions of the NIRC, the business may be eligible to claim input VAT credits or refunds on the VAT paid upon importation. This means that while the initial import VAT is 12%, businesses can recover this cost if they meet the criteria for zero-rated export sales.
